comments.body:
Measurement, 2026-11-03 (no code changed). The clone copy does not reproduce the production hold; the dominant production phase is NOT identified.

## Method

Real clone of `tickets` (own gitdir, no remote; 304,872 commits, 216,266 index entries, 9,885 ticket dirs), checked out at `daa3a65239b^`, the store state just before the Nov 1 sweep. Replayed the production sweep's 10 tickets through the real `compact._run_sweep` on `origin/main` `25bce6c0550`, timing the store-lock hold and every phase inside `_compact_locked`. Second run added a local bare mirror as `origin` (no network) and probed fetch, reconverge and nested lock attempts. Production reads were read-only SSM.

## Clone copy: lock hold per fold

| fold | held (no remote) | held (with mirror remote) | dominant in-lock phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1st (1416) cold reduce caches | 58.1 s | - | `attribution_fields` -> `identity.resolve_current_identity` 56.9 s |
| 1st (1416) warm caches | 11.8 s | 14.4 s | same, 10.7-11.1 s |
| 2nd-10th | 0.49-2.22 s | 0.71-2.73 s | `git add`+`git commit` 0.5-1.1 s; `identify_signer` 0.11 s per signed event |

- `resolve_current_identity` has no identity pointer here (none in production either), so `_match_by_email` reduces every ticket dir to find the git email's identity. It is cached per process (`_ATTRIBUTION_CACHE`), so only the first fold of a sweep pays. Ordinary writes resolve the same attribution BEFORE taking the lock (`finalize_event` runs before `write_and_push`); the fold resolves it inside the lock.
- With a remote: `identify_signer` -> `_keyring_for` -> `rebar.show_ticket` -> `ensure_fresh` runs `git fetch` under the fold's lock, then `sync.reconverge` asks for the store lock the fold already holds and waits out its 2 s pass (2.04 s measured). Throttled to once per 60 s. Filed separately.
- Position map: 111 s, 221,372 entries, outside the lock (as designed).

## Production (read-only), Nov 1 21:00-21:35 PST

- Waiter `held=` values put each fold's acquisition in the same second as the previous fold's COMPACT commit, so nearly the whole commit-to-commit gap was under lock: 160, 176, 176, 186, 220, 237, 243, 248, 250 s.
- The gaps are near-uniform regardless of ticket size: 47c8 folded 14 signed events; a7da, eb95 and f263 folded only CREATE+LINK with no signed events and held 220-243 s.
- Production git on the same clone is fast: index refresh 0.45 s, `diff-index --cached` 0.16 s, no hooks, no stale `index.lock`; 7.79 GiB loose objects in 68k files plus 234 packs; git 2.47.3.
- Host (2 vCPU, no container CPU quota, container memory cap 3.6 GiB): CPU 44-46% user, 15% iowait, 19-42% idle; data-disk reads 33-39 MB/s sustained during the sweep vs 0.4 MB/s before; 240 major faults/s; no swap; no OOM.
- The worker's own log was inside the since-replaced container, so no per-phase production timestamps exist.

## What this establishes

On the clone, the only in-lock phase above 3 s is the first fold's store-wide identity scan, and no fold exceeds the 60 s single-pass budget (cold first fold 58.1 s). Production held each fold 160-250 s, including folds whose in-lock work replays in under 1 s here. Unverified: which phase consumed that time in production. Remaining candidates have not been measured there: the identity scan repeating per fold, network fetch under the lock, and whole-store disk reads under memory pressure.

comments.body:
Change 3269 (Resolve fold lookups before the store lock) removes the clone-measured in-lock costs. It does not establish the production root cause, which stays pending until the next production sweep's timing log.

## Clone replay with the change (same 10 folds, same clone, warm caches)
- First fold: `attribution=12.34s signers=6.40s` now run before the lock; `held=0.78s` (was 11.8 s warm, 58.1 s cold).
- Folds 2-10: `held=0.43-0.69s`; `commit` is 0.41-0.76 s of each hold.
- No fold held the lock longer than 0.78 s, against the 60 s single-pass budget.

## Where the timing line lives
Each fold logs one WARNING line beginning `compaction fold timing: ticket=<id> outcome=<folded|skipped|error>`, followed by the 11 phase durations.
- Production's sweep runs in the async trigger's detached worker, at most once per `compact.trigger_interval_s` (default 6 h), started by a qualifying write. That worker's stderr is `compact-worker.log` in the `.rebar/logs/` directory beside the tracker. With `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, that is `/var/gerrit/site/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` inside the `rebar-mcp-<sha>-8093` container. Read it read-only with `docker exec <container> cat /var/gerrit/site/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` through an SSM `AWS-RunShellScript` payload.
- That path is in the container's own filesystem, not on a volume, so autodeploy's container replacement discards it. Read it after a sweep and before the next deploy. It was 0 bytes after the Nov 3 deploy; before this change the worker installed no log handler, so it would have stayed empty regardless.
- A sweep run inline (`compact.trigger = "always"`) or through `rebar store compact --all` logs the same line to that process's stderr (`journalctl` for the MCP container).

## Reading it
`held` is the whole locked span. If `held` is large and the named in-lock phases (`recover`..`commit`) sum to much less, the time went to work this line does not yet name, and the next check is to time inside that gap. `lock_wait` large means the fold itself queued behind another writer.

comments.author: Rebar Bot Nava
comments.body:
Root cause found, 2026-11-05 (read-only production measurements; fix in review).

## Observation
- Production 2026-11-04 timing lines: the `ledger` phase was 157-277 s of each 158-278 s hold (folds 7773, 1a3b, 26a0, 578a, fb16).
- In the MCP container, on a `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of the live tracker (reads the same object store, writes nothing to it), the exact per-ticket walk `build_ticket_position_commit_map` runs took 160.8 s for 26a0-0104-9b63-4500 (its fold's ledger: 165.50 s) and 266.1 s for fb16-a8b0-c2b7-449a (ledger: 277.48 s).
- The store-wide walk `build_position_commit_map` (the sweep's shared map) took 427.5 s there. Its subprocess timeout is 300 s.
- On the operator clone the same walks take 111 s (store-wide) and 19.1 s (26a0 per-ticket).

## Cause
`build_position_commit_map` times out in production and returns `{}`, so `compact._sweep_position_map` returns `None`. With no map, `_sweep_one_ticket` skips pre-resolution and `_build_authorship_ledger` builds the per-ticket map itself, inside `_fold_under_lock`, under the store write lock. That one `git log --full-history` walk is the ledger phase. The clone replay never reached this branch because its store-wide walk finished inside 300 s. The single-ticket `rebar store compact <id>` path always passed no map, so it always walked under the lock.

## Fix (change pending)
`_compact_locked` resolves positions before `lock.acquire`, like attribution and signers: new `preresolve_positions` builds the per-ticket map when none was passed and fills misses through `preresolve_unmapped_positions`. `_sweep_one_ticket` no longer pre-resolves (the fold does it). The timing line gains a `positions` phase, timed before the lock. No config key, env var, flag or lock added.

Tests (tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py), RED before the fix with `build_ticket_position_commit_map` observed under the lock, GREEN after:
- `test_a_timed_out_sweep_map_runs_no_history_walk_under_the_lock` (store-wide walk raises TimeoutExpired, as in production)
- `test_the_single_ticket_fold_runs_no_history_walk_under_the_lock`

## Separate
Why production git is 4-8x slower than a clone is filed as nickelic-lazuline-gonolek (74,605 loose objects / 8.63 GiB, 235 packs, commit-graph from 2026-08-31). This fix moves the walk out of the lock; it does not make the walk faster.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
On the production MCP host a compaction sweep (`op=compact-sweep`) holds the store write lock 160-280 s per fold. A canonical write waits at most about 181 s (30 s x 2 attempts x 3 passes), so writers fail with `could not acquire lock after 181s ... op=compact-sweep` (2026-11-01 21:03-21:35 PST, evidence on `radiant-benighted-warbler` and `overweak-deviant-shelduck`).

## Root cause
Gerrit 3269 (f1fe7c6f587) added a per-fold timing line. Production sweeps on 2026-11-04 (13:04-13:11 and 17:09-17:17 PST) showed the `ledger` phase was 157-277 s of each 158-278 s hold.
- `_build_authorship_ledger` builds the ticket's position-to-commit map itself (`build_ticket_position_commit_map`, one `git log --full-history` walk) when it receives no map. It runs inside `_fold_under_lock`.
- The sweep shares one store-wide map (`build_position_commit_map`, 300 s subprocess timeout). In production that walk takes 427.5 s, so it returns `{}`, `_sweep_position_map` returns `None`, `_sweep_one_ticket` skips pre-resolution, and every fold walks under the lock. The single-ticket `rebar store compact <id>` path always passes no map.
- Measured in the MCP container on a `git clone --shared` of the live tracker: the per-ticket walk took 160.8 s for 26a0-0104-9b63-4500 (its ledger phase: 165.50 s) and 266.1 s for fb16-a8b0-c2b7-449a (277.48 s).
- The clone replay did not reproduce this because its store-wide walk finished in 111 s, inside the timeout. Production git is 4-8x slower (74,605 loose objects, 235 packs, commit-graph from 2026-08-31), filed as `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`.

Change 3269 also moved two clone-measured in-lock costs before the lock: identity attribution (`resolve_current_identity` reduced every ticket, 11-58 s on the first fold) and signer lookups (`identify_signer` fetched and waited on the held lock, bug `congruent-demurrable-insect`).

## Approach
Follow the compute-before-lock pattern `_compact_locked` already uses for attribution and signers.
1. New `compact_txn.preresolve_positions(ticket_dir, tracker, repo_root, position_commits)`: when no map was passed, build the per-ticket map; then fill misses through `preresolve_unmapped_positions`. `_compact_locked` calls it before `lock.acquire`, timed as a new `positions` phase, and passes the result to the ledger, so the ledger walks no history except for an event written after the prelude (the existing fallback).
2. `compact._sweep_one_ticket` stops pre-resolving; the fold does it for both paths.
Why this fits: it moves the one measured in-lock cost out of the lock with the existing pattern and adds no lock, config key, env var or flag. It does not make the walk faster; that is `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`: `preresolve_positions`, the `positions` phase, prelude call.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`: drop the sweep's own pre-resolution.
- `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py`, `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`: new tests, phase list.
- Earlier, in 3269: `compact_plan.py` (attribution parameter), `compact_trigger.py` (worker stderr handler).

## Testing
State, not duration: each probe records whether the store lock dir exists when a history walk (`build_position_commit_map`, `build_ticket_position_commit_map`, `resolve_event_commit`, `resolve_position_commit`) is called.
- Production shape: the store-wide walk raises `TimeoutExpired`; the sweep folds the ticket, the per-ticket walk runs, none under the lock, and the ledger attributes a late event to its adding commit.
- Single-ticket `compact_cli`: one per-ticket walk, none under the lock, same ledger attribution.
- Regression: every existing test in both files (map reuse, per-ticket fallback count, merge-only and timed-out positions, ledger parity) and all `-k compact` unit tests pass; `make verify` exits 0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Identity attribution and signer lookups run before the store write lock: `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py` observes the lock dir at every `_match_by_email` and `identify_signer` call and finds none under the lock.
- [x] While the fold holds the lock it runs no `git fetch`, no `sync.reconverge` and no second `lock.acquire`: checked by the remote-backed test in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`.
- [x] The SNAPSHOT's `author_id`/`author_email` and the authorship ledger are unchanged by pre-resolution: checked by the equality tests in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`.
- [x] Each fold logs exactly one WARNING timing line naming every phase in `FOLD_PHASES`, including a fold that skips inside the lock, and the detached sweep worker writes it to its stderr log: checked by the timing tests in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`.
- [x] [non-codebase] The production hold is diagnosed from the timing lines: the 2026-11-04 production folds' timing lines and the per-ticket walk times measured in the MCP container are recorded in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=production MCP host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, rebar-mcp container; principal=operator via AWS SSM; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — read via SSM AWS-RunShellScript; the evidence is production log output and timings, not repository files.
- [x] No history walk runs under the store write lock when the sweep's store-wide map fails or when a single ticket is folded: `test_a_timed_out_sweep_map_runs_no_history_walk_under_the_lock` and `test_the_single_ticket_fold_runs_no_history_walk_under_the_lock` in `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py` pass, and failed before the fix.
- [x] [non-codebase] Production confirms the fix: in the first production sweep after the change deploys, every fold's `compaction fold timing` line shows `held` well under 181 s, and the values are recorded in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=production MCP container rebar-mcp-0f409b946e4e-8093 on host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, build 0f409b946e4; principal=operator session via SSM AWS-RunShellScript under the instance role; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — 2026-11-09: the first post-deploy --all sweep (10:48 PST) folded nothing (0 of 10,088 over threshold); the operator-approved sweep-path run at 11:50-11:58 PST (REBAR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=9, --limit=1) folded 029a-c2e8-b4af-44db with held=1.05s (ledger=0.00s, positions=149.28s before the lock), recorded in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=production MCP host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, rebar-mcp container; principal=operator via AWS SSM; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=SSM AWS-RunShellScript journalctl -t rebar-mcp — the evidence is production log output, not repository files.
